rows.name: FESTIVAL WALK
rows.nextWork: Identify the remaining intersected source faces and resolve the existing runtime exception with source-backed component evidence; keep paired secondary support unresolved until its contact proof is complete.
rows.observation: Exact ObjectID/CSUID, 99.744% target coverage, 4.213% excess and no unrelated overlap support the original podium identity. Joint preparation fixes the earlier single-candidate neighbour false hold. All 18,484 source faces have terrain coverage with no fully buried faces after the previously computed 3.183 m2 parent preservation; all 91 neighbours pass. Minimum drawn clearance remains -0.835 m, beyond the ordinary -0.5 m runtime gate, so the full-face foundation result does not independently authorise installation.

rows.name: Festival Walk
rows.nextWork: Classify the failed rim regions using exact source connected components and surface intersections; distinguish supported interface from intentional overhangs, then rerun pair runtime and browser acceptance. Do not lift, crop or remodel either source.
rows.observation: Exact paired Festival Walk source identity passes coverage/excess checks. Joint foundation covers all 16,522 faces with no burial. The earlier 86 contact vertices and broad hull are not full support proof: the new rim/edge diagnostic has 1,224 samples, 605 contacts, 212 without vertical support and a maximum 26.518 m gap. Some are possible overhangs; the evidence does not prove a corrupt model.

The new diagnostic finds 74 contacts of 144 samples, 16 without vertical support and penetration to -7.480 m. This differs from a simple tower-on-flat-podium relationship.
